sections.h2: Where to record and office hours
sections.html:
Luzerne County deeds are recorded in Wilkes-Barre. The public counter of the Recorder of Deeds is in the Courthouse Annex at 153 N. River Street. Mail goes to 200 N. River Street, Wilkes-Barre, PA 18711, and the phone is 570-825-1641. The counter is open Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., except holidays, and the last filings are taken at 4:20 p.m.

A second counter in Hazleton is open only Tuesdays and Thursdays, 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. It takes no cash, only money orders, cashier's checks, personal or business checks, and credit cards, and you wait there while staff finish the documents. Electronic recording can be submitted at any hour.

The Assessors' Office is in the same annex. Every deed needs a certified parcel number before it can be recorded, so the two stops go together.

Under the schedule effective November 17, 2025, the base charge for a deed or a mortgage is $72.75. That covers up to four pages, four names and one PIN. Since July 1, 2026 the county also adds $15.00 to deeds, exempt deeds and mortgages to fund a demolition program for blighted buildings. Ask the office for the exact total on your document.

Luzerne County recording fees, base amounts effective November 17, 2025
DocumentBase fee
Deed$72.75
Mortgage$72.75
Satisfaction$64.75
Release of mortgage$64.75
Assignment of mortgage$64.75
Deed easement or right of way$64.75
Timber conveyance$33.50
Power of attorney$23.50

Smaller charges to watch for:

  • Each page over four costs $2.00, and each name over four costs $0.50.
  • Each PIN after the first costs $0.50 at the Recorder. The Assessor's Office bills its own fee to certify each PIN, so call 570-825-1525 for that amount.
  • A rejected document costs $10.00 by mail and $5.00 when sent electronically.
  • A returned check costs $35.00.
  • One check can cover at most 10 documents, and an overpayment is not refunded. The office either sends the check back for a corrected one or keeps the extra.

The state charges 1 percent, and the county schedule gives the combined rate by municipality. The total is 2 percent everywhere except three places: Wilkes-Barre and Pittston at 3.5 percent and Kingston Borough at 2.5 percent. Hazleton's total is 2 percent. The county has 76 municipalities, so confirm which borough, city or township your house is in before you work out what you will net.

Both the person selling and the person buying are liable to the state for the tax. The Pennsylvania Department of Revenue exempts certain family transfers, transfers by will or intestacy, and transfers to government units. A deed claiming an exemption should say why, for example parent and child. A non-family exemption needs a Statement of Value.

If a property sits in two municipalities, the deed has to state what percentage lies in each, because the local portion is split between them.

Every deed, mortgage and assignment must carry a PIN certified by the Assessor's Office and a signed, certified address for the grantee or mortgagee. Have the Assessor certify the number in the top margin, and leave a blank 2 1/2 inch margin at the bottom of at least two pages for the recording stamps.

  • Statement of Value (REV-183): one original and one copy, completed with the school district, assessed value and common level ratio, then signed and dated by someone connected to the transaction. It counts as a page, and attached exhibits cost $2.00 a page too.
  • Numbering: when several documents make up one transaction, number them in the order they should be recorded. If they arrive in the wrong order, the presenter pays for re-recording.
  • Self-addressed stamped envelopes for returning documents and receipts.
  • No non-standard financing forms, and no blanket assignments or blanket releases, which are refused.

Common level ratios effective July 1 of 2024, 2025 and 2026 are posted with the office's related documents. Use the one in effect on the date of transfer.

There are three online routes. Landex Remote is a prepaid account that draws down as you view records, with images from 1968 to the present and indexing from December 1980. Landex Webstore lets you search the indices free and charges for each document you view or print. IQS Infodex, at searchiqs.com/paluze, is free for older deeds from 1786 to 1967 and also holds grantor and grantee indices from 1786 to August 1, 1993.

Certified copies are made only at the office. A plain copy by mail costs $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each added page. Staff do not run title searches for individuals or give legal or tax advice, so title work stays with an attorney or title company.

Landex also offers a free Record Alert service. It watches up to five PINs or names and emails you when a document is recorded against them. It cannot stop a filing, since the office must record any properly executed document that comes with payment, but it gives an owner early warning of a fraudulent deed. Sellers who still own other parcels, or who inherited property, can sign up while the title is in transition.

sections.h2: From closing table to the record
sections.html:
Most sellers never visit the counter, because the title company or attorney handles the filing. The order of events is the same either way. The Assessor's Office certifies the PIN on the deed, the Statement of Value and the signed grantee address are put with it, and the package goes to the Recorder with one payment covering the recording fee, the county charge and the transfer tax. Electronic submission avoids the trip and the wait at either counter, and a rejected electronic filing costs less than a rejected paper one.

If you do file yourself, check each item in the list above first, bring a check made out correctly, and include the stamped return envelopes. A missed margin or a wrong page order sends the deed back and costs you the rejection fee plus another round.

sections.h2: Before you sell in Luzerne County
sections.html: Luzerne County is a home rule county with 76 municipalities, and Wilkes-Barre, Hazleton, Kingston, Nanticoke and Pittston are its largest places. The 2020 census counted 325,594 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 332,126. Your address decides the transfer tax and the yearly tax, so check the municipality and school district on your tax bill before you quote a net figure to a buyer.

faqs.q: How much is the base fee to record a deed in Luzerne County?
faqs.a: The base fee is $72.75 on the schedule effective November 17, 2025, with $15.00 added from July 1, 2026 for the county demolition fund. The office can confirm the current total.

faqs.q: What is the realty transfer tax rate in Luzerne County?
faqs.a: The county lists a 2 percent total in most municipalities. Wilkes-Barre and Pittston are 3.5 percent, and Kingston Borough is 2.5 percent.

faqs.q: Can I pay for Luzerne County recording with cash?
faqs.a: The Hazleton counter takes no cash, only checks, money orders, cashier's checks and cards. Ask the Wilkes-Barre counter before you bring cash there.

faqs.q: Does Luzerne County require a Statement of Value?
faqs.a: One is required when a deed claims a non-family exemption. File one original and one copy, completed, signed and dated.

faqs.q: How can I find an old Luzerne County deed?
faqs.a: Search Landex for records from 1968 forward, or the free IQS Infodex site for deeds from 1786 to 1967. Certified copies must be requested at the office in person.
